Draw a thin red (#CC3333) rectangle outline (no fill) framing the entire slide edge, inset slightly so the frame is fully visible. 3. Draw a light gray (#E8E8E8) filled band spanning the full slide width across the top ~0-15% of the height. 4. Place a light blue (#CCE5FF) filled rectangle with a dark blue (#0000CC) outline at top-left, spanning ~10-38% of slide width and ~8-22% of slide height so it overlaps both the gray band and the content box top edge; center one line of bold black (#000000) sans-serif text inside it: 'Feature Invariants' (largest text on the slide). 5. Place a yellow (#FFFF99) filled circle with a dark (#333333) outline at the top-right corner (~90-95% width, inside the header band); center small dark text '33' in it. 6. Draw a second thin red (#CC3333) rectangle outline with white fill framing the content area: ~7-93% of slide width and ~20-95% of slide height. 7. Inside the content box near its top (~22-38% height), add one left-aligned line: 'Features Invariants are ' in bold red (#CC0000) immediately followed by 'Problem dependent' in italic, underlined black (#000000); keep the verbatim wording 'Features Invariants' (not 'Feature'). 8. Below the header line, on the left side of the content box (~12-45% width, ~40-70% height), add exactly four bullets stacked vertically, left-aligned, each with a small round bullet marker and regular-weight black (#000000) text, in this order: 'Rotation Invariant', 'Scaling Invariant', 'Translation invariant' (lowercase 'i', verbatim), 'Mirroring Invariant'. 9. Verify there are no images, equations, or charts and that all four bullets are fully visible (static, fully built slide).
